Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 November 2026

OpenLog is an open-source, non-commercial Android app maintained by Rwitesh Bera. This policy covers the app and public website.

Information stored on your device

OpenLog does not require an account or provide cloud sync. It stores your timeline on your device so you can create, search, and view entries. Stored information includes entry text, dates, tags, locations, photos, recordings, attachments, your optional profile name, app preferences, and unsaved drafts.

Some photos stay as original files. They can contain metadata such as capture time or location. OpenLog stores selected media in app storage.

Analytics and error reports

OpenLog uses PostHog for analytics and error reports in the Android app. Events record screen names, app activity, entry actions, media counts, recording duration, backup counts and size, location use, app-lock changes, and notification choices. The app does not ask for analytics consent or provide an in-app way to turn analytics off.

PostHog receives a generated installation ID, app and device details, and the IP address of each request. The ID does not contain your name, but it lets PostHog link events from the same installation. The IP address can indicate an approximate region. This data is pseudonymous, not anonymous. PostHog processes analytics in the United States.

Regular usage events do not contain entry text, photos, recordings, attachment names, or exact location coordinates. Error reports can contain technical details. An app-open event can include a link that opened the app. Do not put private information in an app link. OpenLog does not record screen video or taps. PostHog's retention period follows its service settings.

Read the PostHog privacy policy.

Location

When you choose to add or refresh a location, Android gets your current or recent location and uses its geocoding service to return a place label. That service can receive your coordinates. OpenLog saves the coordinates and place label with your entry or draft. The app does not track your location in the background. Analytics record location use, not your coordinates.

Fonts and website

If you choose an optional font, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN. The request includes the font file and standard connection information, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content. The app keeps the font on your device until you remove it or remove the app.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The site requests fonts from Google Fonts. GitHub and Google receive normal website and font request information. The site source does not include analytics or cookie code. Read the GitHub privacy statement and Google Privacy Policy.

Permissions and notifications

  • OpenLog requests photo access when you choose an image.
  • It requests microphone access when you start a recording.
  • It requests foreground location when you choose to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker lets you choose attachments and backups.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app shows local backup and import updates. A completion notice can show an entry count and backup size. Your device settings control whether these notices appear on the lock screen. OpenLog does not send remote push notifications.

Backups and sharing

An exported backup contains your entries, tags, locations, profile name, preferences, attachments, and media. OpenLog compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. You choose where to save or share it. The chosen folder, service, or app receives the copy.

**Considering app styling decisions**

I’m thinking about the app's consent process and how we use ID instead of names, plus the need for clearer, less technical language. I want to update the CSS for system fonts, particularly within the `.legal` block. We might remove the global Google import since it isn't necessary, and switch to system fonts like Georgia, as system fonts keep things simple and consistent. Maybe we should apply this only to legal pages to maintain uniformity across styles.

**Optimizing font privacy features**

I'm considering using root variables for system fonts to improve privacy and matching local products. This change would affect all web pages, which is great for local-first privacy. The homepage uses DM Serif with a fallback to Georgia, while the body uses DM Sans, which can be simplified. I should note that removing the CSS import means we avoid Google font requests, enhancing privacy. Plus, I see some files still reference Google fonts; we could restructure to avoid this entirely and focus just on website uploads without those imports.

**Updating font variables and policies**

I’m planning to remove the CSS import and update the root font variables. The dark styling under `:root` remains unaffected, but I’ll set the body font to system defaults like `system-ui, -apple-system`, and Georgia for headings. By removing the import, the website stops requesting Google Fonts, which is a privacy win! I’ll also update the policy regarding fonts to reflect that the app optionally uses jsDelivr and the website on GitHub Pages will have no Google Fonts or cookie analytics.

edits.newText: The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. The repository has an iOS backup configuration, but the owner confirms that no iOS app has launched. The current policy did not explain Android backup behavior.

edits.oldText: The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. The website stylesheet requests Google Fonts, and GitHub Pages hosts the site. content.text:
# Privacy audit

**Local working notes. Do not publish.**

**Audit date:** 13 November 2026

**Status:** Static code review. The policy draft needs owner confirmation and legal review before publication.

## Scope and limits

I reviewed app source, configuration, database schemas, permissions, analytics, backup flows, public pages, legal text, and release workflows. I traced data that the app stores, sends, exports, shares, or deletes.

I did not inspect `.env`, remote EAS variables, PostHog project configuration, store privacy forms, vendor contracts, or hosting logs. The owner confirms that the production EAS build includes the PostHog token. I did not capture live network traffic or test the app on a device or emulator. This report is not a legal opinion.

## Owner facts

The owner confirms that OpenLog is a solo-maintained, open-source, non-commercial Android app. No iOS or web app has launched. The owner says the Android app is available in most countries, with some exclusions, but did not give a complete territory list.

A local Google Play installed-audience CSV shows daily totals and selected country columns. It does not identify all available or excluded countries. Do not use it as a full distribution list.

## Confirmed data flows

- **Entries and preferences:** SQLite stores entry text, dates, tags, location coordinates and labels, attachment references, the local profile name, and preferences. A full-text index stores entry text and location labels for local search. [Schema](../src/services/db/migrations/v1.ts#L4-L38), [entry storage](../src/services/db/entries.ts#L21-L42), [search index](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L72-L98), and [preference storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L14-L105).
- **Drafts and media:** App document storage holds media files, optional downloaded fonts, and draft files. A draft can contain text, tags, dates, locations, file names, and copies of selected media. [Media storage](../src/services/media/storage.ts#L8-L14), [draft storage](../src/services/drafts/store.ts#L29-L44), and [draft serialization](../src/services/drafts/snapshot.ts#L5-L16).
- **Profile and app lock:** The optional profile name is stored in SQLite. The app stores only an app-lock flag in SecureStore. The OS handles biometric or passcode checks. [Profile storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L75-L105), [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56), and [local authentication](../src/services/auth/auth.ts#L19-L41).
- **Permissions:** The app requests photo-library access when a person selects images. It requests microphone access when recording starts. It requests foreground location after a person selects the location control. Notifications are requested shortly after the timeline opens. [Media picker](../src/modules/compose/hooks/useMediaAttachments.ts#L45-L68), [recording](../src/services/audio/useRecording.ts#L46-L79), [location](../src/services/location/location.ts#L120-L145), and [timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39).
- **Location:** The app passes coordinates to the native reverse-geocoding API after a person asks for a place label. It stores the coordinates and returned label with a draft or entry. It does not request background location. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L145).
- **Analytics:** A build sends PostHog events only when it has a project token and is not in JavaScript development mode. The client uses the US endpoint, captures app lifecycle events, and enables JavaScript exception and unhandled-rejection capture. Interaction autocapture and session replay are off. [PostHog configuration](../src/config/posthog.ts#L1-L25), [screen tracking](../App.tsx#L103-L129), and [event calls](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).
- **Other network requests:** Selecting an optional font downloads a file from jsDelivr. The public website loads Google Fonts. GitHub Pages hosts the website. [Font source](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [website stylesheet](../webpage/style.css#L1), and [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L1-L36).
- **Build and distribution:** GitHub Actions requests Android builds from EAS and uploads them to Google Play. The workflow has no path to runtime entries. Store-side data collection was not reviewed. [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L74-L121).
- **Backups and sharing:** A manual backup contains timeline rows, tags, preferences, locations, and referenced media. The app compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. Users choose a folder or share target. [Backup export](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L239) and [export handling](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L109-L187).
- **System backups:** Android Auto Backup is enabled. The rules include shared-preference files and exclude the database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. The iOS configuration has no backup exclusion, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. [Android app declaration](../app.json#L27-L42), [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L8-L38), and [EAS app declaration](../app.json#L11-L25).
- **Not found:** The tracked app source has no account backend, cloud-sync API, ad SDK, remote push-token registration, or website analytics script. The website source has no cookie code. [Dependencies](../package.json#L1-L43) and [website home page](../webpage/index.html#L1-L116). These findings do not cover hosting-provider behavior or data that users send by email.

## Findings

### F1. High: Analytics disclosure does not match the full data flow

The version of `webpage/privacy-policy.html` on `main` called analytics anonymous and said it did not collect location. This draft replaces those claims. The PostHog SDK creates a persistent pseudonymous identifier and attaches app, device, operating-system, locale, time-zone, and screen details. The app sends `location_used` and `has_location` events, but it does not send GPS coordinates or place labels as event fields. The SDK also exposes the request IP to PostHog. The app does not turn off the IP-based location estimate in PostHog. The owner confirms PostHog stores analytics in the United States. [Current policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L3-L23), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry events](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

The app has no analytics consent prompt or opt-out. The privacy screen contains app lock, backup, and storage controls only. The owner confirms the production token is set. Its value remains outside the repository. [Privacy screen](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L389-L464), [EAS profile](../eas.json#L7-L25), [environment template](../.env.example#L1), and [development guide](../DEVELOPMENT.md#L15-L18).

### F2. High: Error reports and launch URLs are not fully scrubbed

The app enables capture of unhandled JavaScript errors and rejected promises. `PostHogErrorBoundary` also sends error details and a component stack. Manual reports replace file paths with `<path>`, but automatic reports do not use that helper. The PostHog lifecycle event can also include the app launch URL. No global filter or launch-URL scrubber appears in the app configuration. I found no confirmed content leak, but an exception message or URL can contain personal information. [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L11-L19), [error boundary](../App.tsx#L121-L129), [app scheme](../app.json#L5-L12), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), and [manual error reporting](../src/shared/utils/devLog.ts#L11-L39).

### F3. High: Local storage, backups, and app lock need clearer limits

The Android app uses SQLite and app files without an application-level encryption layer. The app lock calls the device authentication prompt, but it does not encrypt entries or attachments. The source also notes that the operating system can take an app-switcher snapshot before the JavaScript cover appears. [Database](../src/services/db/database.ts#L1-L28), [app lock](../src/services/auth/useAppLock.ts#L22-L47), and [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56).

The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. iOS app data has no configured backup exclusion. The current policy did not explain these paths. [Export archive](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L132), [export cleanup](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L320-L324), [share fallback](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L137-L171), and [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L12-L38).

### F4. Medium: Location, font, website, and contact requests need disclosure

A location action sends coordinates to the native geocoder. iOS uses Core Location. Android calls the Android Geocoder API, but the repository does not name its downstream provider. The policy did not describe this request. The existing review file already lists this gap as P3-5. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L85) and [open review finding](./review-findings.md#L9-L17).

The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. The website stylesheet requests Google Fonts, and GitHub Pages hosts the site. A person who emails the listed Gmail address sends their message and any attached files to that mailbox. The code does not define retention for website logs or email. [Font resolver](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [site CSS](../webpage/style.css#L1), [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L17-L36), and [contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

### F5. Medium: Permission timing and attachment metadata need review

The app requests notification permission shortly after the timeline opens, not when a person starts a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The unused iOS configuration declares photo-library write use, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The reviewed app code opens a share sheet and does not call a photo-library write API. The image path can keep the original file, so embedded metadata can remain. [Timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39), [notification content](../src/services/notifications/notifications.ts#L65-L94), [iOS permission string](../app.json#L14-L25), [image path](../src/services/media/images.ts#L11-L48), and [share action](../src/services/media/share.ts#L15-L32).

The attachment picker accepts any file type. It can open selected files in another app. The policy did not describe file-provider or share-target handling. [Document picker](../src/services/media/attachments.ts#L20-L68).

The privacy contact uses a Gmail address. The code does not define mailbox-provider retention or how the owner handles requests. [Contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

### F6. Medium: Public claims are broader than the implementation

The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. The terms say local content is not uploaded or synced. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, font requests, system backups, and user-selected sharing. The old policy also promised practical notice for material changes, but no in-app notice path appears in the app. [README](../README.md#L7-L15), [website](../webpage/index.html#L85-L102), [About screen](../src/screens/settings/AboutSettings.tsx#L79-L84), and [terms](../webpage/terms.html#L27-L38).

The product guide says analytics never include locations. The app sends location-use and location-presence events. These events do not contain exact coordinates, so the guide and event design need a shared definition of location data. [Product guide](../AGENTS.md#L13-L16), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry event fields](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

### F7. Medium: Retention, rights, operator, age, and jurisdiction are unknown

The app sets no local content expiry and has no single control that clears entries, profile details, preferences, font files, and analytics state. Delete-all removes entries, tags, and drafts. It tries to remove unreferenced media, but leaves profile and app preferences. SQLite deletion does not promise secure erasure. PostHog retention, website log retention, and email retention are not defined in the repository. [Delete-all action](../src/modules/entry/store/EntryStore.ts#L139-L147), [privacy settings](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L375-L386), and [database setup](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L33-L50).

The previous policy said OpenLog is not directed to children under 13, but the app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner identifies Rwitesh Bera as the individual maintainer and says no company is registered. The exact age range, full territory list, postal address, and privacy-request process remain unknown. The repository does not contain a Google Play Data Safety declaration. [Policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [public contact and terms](../webpage/terms.html#L63-L79), [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L1-L20), and [iOS config](../app.json#L11-L25).

## Recommendations

1. Confirm the production PostHog token, data region, GeoIP behavior, retention, processor terms, subprocessors, and deletion process.
2. Add a user-facing analytics choice or confirm that analytics run by default. Update the policy and store disclosures to match.
3. Disable launch-URL capture unless the app needs it. Add a tested event scrubber for exception text, stack traces, paths, and query values.
4. Decide whether to add encryption for local content and backup archives. Protect app-switcher snapshots before the JavaScript cover appears, or document this limit. Document Android backup behavior. Review iOS backups before an iOS launch. Remove temporary export files on every exit path.
5. Confirm the Android geocoder provider. Keep location use explicit and document that the platform geocoder receives coordinates.
6. Remove the unused photo-library write permission or add and document the feature that needs it. Use the narrowest photo-picker access available. Remove photo metadata before storage or explain that it can remain.
7. Move the notification prompt to a backup action. Limit completion details that appear on lock screens.
8. Self-host website fonts or disclose Google Fonts requests. Document GitHub Pages and contact-mail retention.
9. Align the README, website, About screen, terms, and product guide with the confirmed data flows.
10. Define retention, deletion, and privacy-request steps. Confirm the legal operator, address, age range, user countries, supported platforms, and notice process before publication.

## Owner clarifications

1. What PostHog retention period, GeoIP configuration, data-processing terms, and subprocessor list apply? Who handles deletion requests?
2. Does the owner want automatic error and launch-link capture? What legal basis and user choice apply to analytics and location requests?
3. What postal contact address and email-retention period belong in the policy?
4. What age groups does OpenLog serve? What countries does Google Play make the app available in, and which countries are excluded?
5. What data can Android shared preferences contain? Does the owner intend Android cloud backup and device transfer?
6. Which service resolves Android coordinates? What service terms and retention apply to coordinates sent by the platform geocoder?
7. Does any supported feature save photos directly to the photo library? What rules apply to attachment metadata and files selected from cloud providers?
8. What privacy-request and notice processes does the owner use? Does any business practice share or sell data beyond the flows in this repository?

## Regulatory review

The repository does not establish the country of the operator, user countries, age range, or business thresholds. This review cannot decide which laws apply. Counsel must assess the launch markets. Candidate laws include GDPR, UK GDPR, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act of India, US state privacy laws, and COPPA. Counsel must assess COPPA if the service targets children or the owner knows a child under 13 uses it.

Use data minimization, purpose limits, retention limits, and privacy by design as review criteria. Use the NIST Privacy Framework for a follow-up privacy review and OWASP MASVS for mobile security review. Confirm Google Play Data Safety and Apple App Privacy disclosures against the final build. This code review does not establish compliance with any law or framework.

Backups and sharing

An exported backup contains your entries, tags, locations, profile name, preferences, attachments, and media. OpenLog compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. You choose where to save or share it. The chosen folder, service, or app receives the copy.

Android system backup can copy some app preferences. OpenLog's backup rules exclude the timeline database, media, and drafts. System backup settings control whether included preferences are copied. When you share a photo or open a file in another app, that app receives the selected file.

Retention and deletion

Saved entries and media stay on your device until you delete them or remove the app. Unsaved drafts stay until you save or discard them. Delete all entries removes entries, tags, and drafts. It also tries to remove media that no remaining entry uses. It does not remove your profile name or preferences.

Exported backups, shared files, and system backup copies remain until you or their storage provider deletes them. The app does not promise secure erasure of deleted database data.

Security

The optional app lock uses your device's biometric or passcode prompt. It does not encrypt entries, media, drafts, or backup files. Protection also depends on your device and its settings.

Children and privacy requests

OpenLog is not directed to children under 13.

Privacy rights depend on where you live. Contact us to ask about a privacy request. OpenLog has no account and keeps no central copy of your timeline.

Fonts and website

If you choose an optional font, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN. The request includes the font file and standard connection information, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content. The app keeps the font on your device until you remove it or remove the app.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The site uses system fonts and has no analytics or cookie code. GitHub receives normal page request information, such as your IP address. Read the GitHub privacy statement .

Permissions and notifications

  • OpenLog requests photo access when you choose an image.
  • It requests microphone access when you start a recording.
  • It requests foreground location when you choose to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker lets you choose attachments and backups.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app shows local backup and import updates. A completion notice can show an entry count and backup size. /bin/bash: line 1: .openlog: command not found
17:The owner confirms that OpenLog is a solo-maintained, open-source, non-commercial Android app. No iOS or web app has launched. The owner says the Android app is available in most countries, with some exclusions, but did not give a complete territory list.
19:A local Google Play installed-audience CSV shows daily totals and selected country columns. It does not identify all available or excluded countries. Do not use it as a full distribution list.
29:- **Other network requests:** Selecting an optional font downloads a file from jsDelivr. GitHub Pages hosts the public website, which now uses system fonts. A separate database-migration diagram imports Google Fonts but is not part of the Pages deployment. [Font source](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [website stylesheet](../webpage/style.css#L1), [migration diagram](../src/services/db/migrations/overview.html#L1-L10), and [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L1-L36).
31:- **Backups and sharing:** A manual backup contains timeline rows, tags, preferences, locations, and referenced media. The app compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. Users choose a folder or share target. [Backup export](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L239) and [export handling](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L109-L187).
32:- **System backups:** Android Auto Backup is enabled. The rules include shared-preference files and exclude the database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. The iOS configuration has no backup exclusion, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. [Android app declaration](../app.json#L27-L42), [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L8-L38), and [EAS app declaration](../app.json#L11-L25).
45:The app enables capture of unhandled JavaScript errors and rejected promises. `PostHogErrorBoundary` also sends error details and a component stack. Manual reports replace file paths with `<path>`, but automatic reports do not use that helper. The PostHog lifecycle event can also include the app launch URL. No global filter or launch-URL scrubber appears in the app configuration. I found no confirmed content leak, but an exception message or URL can contain personal information. [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L11-L19), [error boundary](../App.tsx#L121-L129), [app scheme](../app.json#L5-L12), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), and [manual error reporting](../src/shared/utils/devLog.ts#L11-L39).
51:The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. iOS app data has no configured backup exclusion. The current policy did not explain these paths. [Export archive](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L132), [export cleanup](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L320-L324), [share fallback](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L137-L171), and [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L12-L38).
53:### F4. Medium: Location, font, website, and contact requests need disclosure
61:The app requests notification permission shortly after the timeline opens, not when a person starts a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The unused iOS configuration declares photo-library write use, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The reviewed app code opens a share sheet and does not call a photo-library write API. The image path can keep the original file, so embedded metadata can remain. [Timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39), [notification content](../src/services/notifications/notifications.ts#L65-L94), [iOS permission string](../app.json#L14-L25), [image path](../src/services/media/images.ts#L11-L48), and [share action](../src/services/media/share.ts#L15-L32).
77:The previous policy said OpenLog is not directed to children under 13, but the app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner identifies Rwitesh Bera as the individual maintainer and says no company is registered. The exact age range, full territory list, postal address, and privacy-request process remain unknown. The repository does not contain a Google Play Data Safety declaration. [Policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [public contact and terms](../webpage/terms.html#L63-L79), [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L1-L20), and [iOS config](../app.json#L11-L25).
105:The repository does not establish the country of the operator, user countries, age range, or business thresholds. This review cannot decide which laws apply. Counsel must assess the launch markets. Candidate laws include GDPR, UK GDPR, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act of India, US state privacy laws, and COPPA. Counsel must assess COPPA if the service targets children or the owner knows a child under 13 uses it.
107:Use data minimization, purpose limits, retention limits, and privacy by design as review criteria. Use the NIST Privacy Framework for a follow-up privacy review and OWASP MASVS for mobile security review. Confirm Google Play Data Safety for the Android build. Review Apple App Privacy before any iOS launch. This code review does not establish compliance with any law or framework.

edits.oldText: The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. The terms say local content is not uploaded or synced. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, font requests, system backups, and user-selected sharing. The old policy also promised practical notice for material changes, but no in-app notice path appears in the app.
edits.newText: The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, system backups, and user-selected sharing. The earlier terms also made a broad no-upload claim. The revised terms remove that claim. The prior policy promised practical notice for material changes, but the app has no in-app notice path.

This report is not a legal opinion. docs/privacy-audit.md:17:The owner confirms that OpenLog is a solo-maintained, open-source, non-commercial Android app. No iOS or web app has launched. The client uses the US endpoint, captures app lifecycle events, and enables JavaScript exception and unhandled-rejection capture. Interaction autocapture and session replay are off. [PostHog configuration](../src/config/posthog.ts#L1-L25), [screen tracking](../App.tsx#L103-L129), and [event calls](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224). docs/privacy-audit.md:29:- **Other network requests:** Selecting an optional font downloads a file from jsDelivr. GitHub Pages hosts the public website, which now uses system fonts. A separate database-migration diagram imports Google Fonts but is not part of the Pages deployment. [Font source](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [website stylesheet](../webpage/style.css#L1), [migration diagram](../src/services/db/migrations/overview.html#L1-L10), and [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L1-L36). docs/privacy-audit.md:32:- **System backups:** Android Auto Backup is enabled. The rules include shared-preference files and exclude the database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. The iOS configuration has no backup exclusion, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. [Android app declaration](../app.json#L27-L42), [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L8-L38), and [EAS app declaration](../app.json#L11-L25). docs/privacy-audit.md:39:The version of `webpage/privacy-policy.html` on `main` called analytics anonymous and said it did not collect location. This draft replaces those claims. The PostHog SDK creates a persistent pseudonymous identifier and attaches app, device, operating-system, locale, time-zone, and screen details. The app sends `location_used` and `has_location` events, but it does not send GPS coordinates or place labels as event fields. The SDK also exposes the request IP to PostHog. The app does not turn off the IP-based location estimate in PostHog. The owner confirms PostHog stores analytics in the United States. [Current policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L3-L23), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry events](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224). docs/privacy-audit.md:45:The app enables capture of unhandled JavaScript errors and rejected promises. `PostHogErrorBoundary` also sends error details and a component stack. Manual reports replace file paths with ``, but automatic reports do not use that helper. The PostHog lifecycle event can also include the app launch URL. No global filter or launch-URL scrubber appears in the app configuration. I found no confirmed content leak, but an exception message or URL can contain personal information. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. The iOS configuration has no backup exclusion, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The policy did not explain Android backup behavior. [Export archive](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L132), [export cleanup](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L320-L324), [share fallback](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L137-L171), and [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L12-L38). docs/privacy-audit.md:55:A location action in the Android app sends coordinates to the native geocoder. The repository does not name its downstream provider. iOS configuration uses Core Location, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The policy did not describe the Android request. The existing review file lists this gap as P3-5. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L85) and [open review finding](./review-findings.md#L9-L17). docs/privacy-audit.md:57:The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. GitHub Pages hosts the public website, which now uses system fonts. A person who emails the listed Gmail address sends their message and any attached files to that mailbox. The code does not define retention for website logs or email. [Font resolver](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [site CSS](../webpage/style.css#L1), [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L17-L36), and [contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21). docs/privacy-audit.md:61:The app requests notification permission shortly after the timeline opens, not when a person starts a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The unused iOS configuration declares photo-library write use, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The reviewed app code opens a share sheet and does not call a photo-library write API. The image path can keep the original file, so embedded metadata can remain. [Timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39), [notification content](../src/services/notifications/notifications.ts#L65-L94), [iOS permission string](../app.json#L14-L25), [image path](../src/services/media/images.ts#L11-L48), and [share action](../src/services/media/share.ts#L15-L32). docs/privacy-audit.md:69:The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, system backups, and user-selected sharing. Delete-all removes entries, tags, and drafts. It tries to remove unreferenced media, but leaves profile and app preferences. SQLite deletion does not promise secure erasure. PostHog retention, website log retention, and email retention are not defined in the repository. [Delete-all action](../src/modules/entry/store/EntryStore.ts#L139-L147), [privacy settings](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L375-L386), and [database setup](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L33-L50). docs/privacy-audit.md:77:The previous policy said OpenLog is not directed to children under 13, but the app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner identifies Rwitesh Bera as the individual maintainer and says no company is registered. The exact age range, full territory list, postal address, and privacy-request process remain unknown. The repository does not contain a Google Play Data Safety declaration. Confirm the production PostHog token, data region, GeoIP behavior, retention, processor terms, subprocessors, and deletion process. docs/privacy-audit.md:84:4. Decide whether to add encryption for local content and backup archives. Protect app-switcher snapshots before the JavaScript cover appears, or document this limit. Document Android backup behavior. Review iOS backup rules before an iOS launch. Remove temporary export files on every exit path. docs/privacy-audit.md:94:1. Candidate laws include GDPR, UK GDPR, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act of India, US state privacy laws, and COPPA. Counsel must assess COPPA if the service targets children or the owner knows a child under 13 uses it. docs/privacy-audit.md:107:Use data minimization, purpose limits, retention limits, and privacy by design as review criteria. **Evaluating GitHub Commit Privacy**

Force pushing modifies the pull request and commit list, but old commits may still be accessible by their SHA if cached. GitHub may retain unreferenced objects, and there's no clean API to purge them. The user might need GitHub Support for this. While the report isn't highly confidential, it may expose some code specifics. For privacy, we'll clear from the pull request view and delete the checkpoint but remember that remote cached commits could remain until garbage collection.

**Confirming User Authorization**

The user said "yes" when asked if I could rewrite PR #17 without the docs/privacy-audit.md file and delete the checkpoint `01M7...`, along with any replacement checkpoints that arose during that work. This consent allows me to remove the full session transcript of the checkpoint, not just the audit report. Now that I have explicit permission to proceed, I can rewrite the branch, commit, push, and delete the checkpoint. I'll consider running a dry run first since the user authorized it and it would be read-only.

List checkpoints on the current branch.

By default shows condensed checkpoints from the checkpoints branch for the
current branch. Use --pending for work that is not a checkpoint yet:

  - A preview of the next checkpoint for each session in this worktree with
    pending work. Agent turns are recorded in session state, not in git, so
    this work has no checkpoint ID until you commit it. The preview shows the
    turns since the last checkpoint, the files touched, subagent task records,
    and the prompts since the last checkpoint.
  - Subagent task records of other sessions on HEAD (not yet condensed).
  - Logs-only resume points recovered from commits whose logs are already
    condensed.

Use --outgoing to see what your next 'git push' sends: the checkpoints
queued for the checkpoint sync remote, read from local state with no network
call. Each one shows its ID, age, agent, first prompt (or summary) and the
files it touched. It needs the git-refs checkpoint backend, which pushes one
ref per checkpoint; the git-branch backend pushes entire/checkpoints/v1 as one
branch, so --outgoing reports an error there.

Output modes:

  --pending           Select the pending dataset described above.
  --pending --json    The pending dataset as a JSON array.
  --outgoing          Select the outgoing dataset described above.
  --outgoing --json   The outgoing dataset as one JSON object.

is_task_checkpoint, is_logs_only, and when set tool_use_id, condensation_id,
session_id and session_prompt. A next-checkpoint preview element has an empty
id, "is_next_checkpoint": true, and a "next_checkpoint" object:

content.text:
The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. The iOS configuration has no backup exclusion, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The policy did not explain Android backup behavior. [Export archive](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L132), [export cleanup](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L320-L324), [share fallback](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L137-L171), and [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L12-L38).

### F4. Medium: Location, font, website, and contact requests need disclosure

A location action in the Android app sends coordinates to the native geocoder. The repository does not name its downstream provider. iOS configuration uses Core Location, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The policy did not describe the Android request. The existing review file lists this gap as P3-5. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L85) and [open review finding](./review-findings.md#L9-L17).

The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. GitHub Pages hosts the public website, which now uses system fonts. A person who emails the listed Gmail address sends their message and any attached files to that mailbox. The code does not define retention for website logs or email. [Font resolver](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [site CSS](../webpage/style.css#L1), [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L17-L36), and [contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

### F5. Medium: Permission timing and attachment metadata need review

The app requests notification permission shortly after the timeline opens, not when a person starts a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The unused iOS configuration declares photo-library write use, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The reviewed app code opens a share sheet and does not call a photo-library write API. The image path can keep the original file, so embedded metadata can remain. [Timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39), [notification content](../src/services/notifications/notifications.ts#L65-L94), [iOS permission string](../app.json#L14-L25), [image path](../src/services/media/images.ts#L11-L48), and [share action](../src/services/media/share.ts#L15-L32).

The attachment picker accepts any file type. It can open selected files in another app. The policy did not describe file-provider or share-target handling. [Document picker](../src/services/media/attachments.ts#L20-L68).

The privacy contact uses a Gmail address. The code does not define mailbox-provider retention or how the owner handles requests. [Contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

### F6. Medium: Public claims are broader than the implementation

The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, system backups, and user-selected sharing. The earlier terms also made a broad no-upload claim. The revised terms remove that claim. The prior policy promised practical notice for material changes, but the app has no in-app notice path. [README](../README.md#L7-L15), [website](../webpage/index.html#L85-L102), [About screen](../src/screens/settings/AboutSettings.tsx#L79-L84), and [terms](../webpage/terms.html#L27-L38).

The product guide says analytics never include locations. The app sends location-use and location-presence events. These events do not contain exact coordinates, so the guide and event design need a shared definition of location data. [Product guide](../AGENTS.md#L13-L16), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry event fields](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

### F7. Medium: Retention, rights, operator, age, and jurisdiction are unknown

The app sets no local content expiry and has no single control that clears entries, profile details, preferences, font files, and analytics state. Delete-all removes entries, tags, and drafts. It tries to remove unreferenced media, but leaves profile and app preferences. SQLite deletion does not promise secure erasure. PostHog retention, website log retention, and email retention are not defined in the repository. [Delete-all action](../src/modules/entry/store/EntryStore.ts#L139-L147), [privacy settings](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L375-L386), and [database setup](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L33-L50).

If you choose an optional font, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN. The request includes the font file and standard connection information, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content. The app keeps the font on your device until you remove it or remove the app.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The site uses system fonts and has no analytics or cookie code. GitHub receives normal page request information, such as your IP address. Read the GitHub privacy statement . The site also links to external services. Their privacy policies apply when you open those links.

Permissions and notifications

  • OpenLog requests photo access when you choose an image.
  • It requests microphone access when you start a recording.
  • It requests foreground location when you choose to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker lets you choose attachments and backups.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app shows local backup and import updates. A completion notice can show an entry count [68 more lines in file. Use offset=103 to continue.]

OpenLog Contact

OpenLog / Privacy Policy

Privacy Policy

Last updated: 13 November 2026

OpenLog is an open-source, non-commercial Android app maintained by Rwitesh Bera. This policy covers the app and public website.

Information stored on your device

OpenLog does not require an account or provide cloud sync. It stores your timeline on your device so you can create, search, and view entries. Stored information includes entry text, dates, tags, locations, photos, recordings, attachments, your optional profile name, app preferences, and unsaved drafts.

Some photos stay as original files. They can contain metadata such as capture time or location. OpenLog stores selected media in app storage.

Analytics and error reports

OpenLog uses PostHog for analytics and error reports in the Android app. Events record screen names, app activity, entry actions, media counts, recording duration, backup counts and size, location use, app-lock changes, and notification choices. The app does not ask for analytics consent or provide an in-app way to turn analytics off.

PostHog receives a generated installation ID, app and device details, and the IP address of each request. These details include app version, device model, operating system, language, and time zone. The ID does not contain your name, but PostHog can link events from the same installation. The IP address can indicate an approximate region. This data is not anonymous. PostHog processes analytics in the United States.

Regular usage events do not contain your profile name, email address, entry text, photos, recordings, attachment names, or exact location coordinates. Error reports can contain technical details. An app-open event can include a link that opened the app. Do not put private information in an app link. OpenLog does not record screen video or taps. PostHog's retention period follows its service settings. Contact us for the current period.

Read the PostHog privacy policy.

Location

When you choose to add or refresh a location, Android gets your current or recent location and uses its geocoding service to return a place label. That service can receive your coordinates. OpenLog saves the coordinates and place label with your entry or draft. The app does not track your location in the background. Analytics record location use, not your coordinates.

Fonts and website

If you choose an optional font, OpenLog downloads it from the jsDelivr CDN. The request includes the font file and standard connection information, such as your IP address. It does not include entry content. The app keeps the font on your device until you remove it or remove the app.

GitHub Pages hosts the OpenLog website. The site uses system fonts and has no analytics or cookie code. GitHub receives normal page request information, such as your IP address. Read the GitHub privacy statement . The site also links to external services. Their privacy policies apply when you open those links.

Permissions and notifications

  • OpenLog requests photo access when you choose an image.
  • It requests microphone access when you start a recording.
  • It requests foreground location when you choose to add or refresh a place.
  • The system file picker lets you choose attachments and backups.

OpenLog asks for notification permission shortly after the timeline opens. If you allow it, the app shows local backup and import updates. A completion notice can show an entry count and backup size. Your device settings control whether these notices appear on the lock screen. OpenLog does not send remote push notifications.

Backups and sharing

An exported backup contains your entries, tags, locations, profile name, preferences, attachments, and media. OpenLog compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. You choose where to save or share it. The chosen folder, service, or app receives the copy.

Android system backup can copy some app preferences. OpenLog's backup rules exclude the timeline database, media, and drafts. System backup settings control whether included preferences are copied. When you share a photo or open a file in another app, that app receives the selected file.

Retention and deletion

Saved entries and media stay on your device until you delete them or remove the app. Unsaved drafts stay until you save or discard them. Delete all entries removes entries, tags, and drafts. It also tries to remove media that no remaining entry uses. It does not remove your profile name or preferences.

Exported backups, shared files, and system backup copies remain until you or their storage provider deletes them. The app does not promise secure erasure of deleted database data.

Security

The optional app lock uses your device's biometric or passcode prompt. It does not encrypt entries, media, drafts, or backup files. Protection also depends on your device and its settings.

Children and privacy requests

OpenLog is not directed to children under 13.

Privacy rights depend on where you live. Contact us to ask about a privacy request. OpenLog has no account and keeps no central copy of your timeline.

Contact and changes

OpenLog is maintained by Rwitesh Bera as an independent project. For privacy questions, email rwiteshbera@gmail.com. Google handles email through Gmail. We use your message to reply. We will update this page when our data practices change.

OpenLog · made by Rwitesh Bera
Changelog Privacy Policy Terms & Conditions

# Privacy audit

**Local working notes. Do not publish.**

**Audit date:** 13 November 2026

**Status:** Static code review. The policy draft needs owner confirmation and legal review before publication.

## Scope and limits

I reviewed app source, configuration, database schemas, permissions, analytics, backup flows, public pages, legal text, and release workflows. I traced data that the app stores, sends, exports, shares, or deletes.

I did not inspect `.env`, remote EAS variables, PostHog project configuration, store privacy forms, vendor contracts, or hosting logs. The owner confirms that the production EAS build includes the PostHog token. I did not capture live network traffic or test the app on a device or emulator. This report is not a legal opinion.

## Owner facts

The owner confirms that OpenLog is a solo-maintained, open-source, non-commercial Android app. No iOS or web app has launched. The owner says the Android app is available in most countries, with some exclusions, but did not give a complete territory list.

A local Google Play installed-audience CSV shows daily totals and selected country columns. It does not identify all available or excluded countries. Do not use it as a full distribution list.

## Confirmed data flows

- **Entries and preferences:** SQLite stores entry text, dates, tags, location coordinates and labels, attachment references, the local profile name, and preferences. A full-text index stores entry text and location labels for local search. [Schema](../src/services/db/migrations/v1.ts#L4-L38), [entry storage](../src/services/db/entries.ts#L21-L42), [search index](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L72-L98), and [preference storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L14-L105).
- **Drafts and media:** App document storage holds media files, optional downloaded fonts, and draft files. A draft can contain text, tags, dates, locations, file names, and copies of selected media. [Media storage](../src/services/media/storage.ts#L8-L14), [draft storage](../src/services/drafts/store.ts#L29-L44), and [draft serialization](../src/services/drafts/snapshot.ts#L5-L16).
- **Profile and app lock:** The optional profile name is stored in SQLite. The app stores only an app-lock flag in SecureStore. The OS handles biometric or passcode checks. [Profile storage](../src/services/db/settings.ts#L75-L105), [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56), and [local authentication](../src/services/auth/auth.ts#L19-L41).
- **Permissions:** The app requests photo-library access when a person selects images. It requests microphone access when recording starts. It requests foreground location after a person selects the location control. Notifications are requested shortly after the timeline opens. [Media picker](../src/modules/compose/hooks/useMediaAttachments.ts#L45-L68), [recording](../src/services/audio/useRecording.ts#L46-L79), [location](../src/services/location/location.ts#L120-L145), and [timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39).
- **Location:** The app passes coordinates to the native reverse-geocoding API after a person asks for a place label. It stores the coordinates and returned label with a draft or entry. It does not request background location. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L145).
- **Analytics:** A build sends PostHog events only when it has a project token and is not in JavaScript development mode. The client uses the US endpoint, captures app lifecycle events, and enables JavaScript exception and unhandled-rejection capture. Interaction autocapture and session replay are off. [PostHog configuration](../src/config/posthog.ts#L1-L25), [screen tracking](../App.tsx#L103-L129), and [event calls](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).
- **Other network requests:** Selecting an optional font downloads a file from jsDelivr. GitHub Pages hosts the public website, which now uses system fonts. A separate database-migration diagram imports Google Fonts but is not part of the Pages deployment. [Font source](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [website stylesheet](../webpage/style.css#L1), [migration diagram](../src/services/db/migrations/overview.html#L1-L10), and [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L1-L36).
- **Build and distribution:** GitHub Actions requests Android builds from EAS and uploads them to Google Play. The workflow has no path to runtime entries. Store-side data collection was not reviewed. [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L74-L121).
- **Backups and sharing:** A manual backup contains timeline rows, tags, preferences, locations, and referenced media. The app compresses the archive but does not encrypt it. Users choose a folder or share target. [Backup export](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L239) and [export handling](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L109-L187).
- **System backups:** Android Auto Backup is enabled. The rules include shared-preference files and exclude the database, media, drafts, and SecureStore preferences. The iOS configuration has no backup exclusion, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. [Android app declaration](../app.json#L27-L42), [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L8-L38), and [EAS app declaration](../app.json#L11-L25).
- **Not found:** The tracked app source has no account backend, cloud-sync API, ad SDK, remote push-token registration, or website analytics script. The website source has no cookie code. [Dependencies](../package.json#L1-L43) and [website home page](../webpage/index.html#L1-L116). These findings do not cover hosting-provider behavior or data that users send by email.

## Findings

### F1. High: Analytics disclosure does not match the full data flow

The version of `webpage/privacy-policy.html` on `main` called analytics anonymous and said it did not collect location. This draft replaces those claims. The PostHog SDK creates a persistent pseudonymous identifier and attaches app, device, operating-system, locale, time-zone, and screen details. The app sends `location_used` and `has_location` events, but it does not send GPS coordinates or place labels as event fields. The SDK also exposes the request IP to PostHog. The app does not turn off the IP-based location estimate in PostHog. The owner confirms PostHog stores analytics in the United States. [Current policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L3-L23), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry events](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

The app has no analytics consent prompt or opt-out. The privacy screen contains app lock, backup, and storage controls only. The owner confirms the production token is set. Its value remains outside the repository. [Privacy screen](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L389-L464), [EAS profile](../eas.json#L7-L25), [environment template](../.env.example#L1), and [development guide](../DEVELOPMENT.md#L15-L18).

### F2. High: Error reports and launch URLs are not fully scrubbed

The app enables capture of unhandled JavaScript errors and rejected promises. `PostHogErrorBoundary` also sends error details and a component stack. Manual reports replace file paths with `<path>`, but automatic reports do not use that helper. The PostHog lifecycle event can also include the app launch URL. No global filter or launch-URL scrubber appears in the app configuration. I found no confirmed content leak, but an exception message or URL can contain personal information. [PostHog setup](../src/config/posthog.ts#L11-L19), [error boundary](../App.tsx#L121-L129), [app scheme](../app.json#L5-L12), [locked SDK version](../pnpm-lock.yaml#L2321-L2332), and [manual error reporting](../src/shared/utils/devLog.ts#L11-L39).

### F3. High: Local storage, backups, and app lock need clearer limits

The Android app uses SQLite and app files without an application-level encryption layer. The app lock calls the device authentication prompt, but it does not encrypt entries or attachments. The source also notes that the operating system can take an app-switcher snapshot before the JavaScript cover appears. [Database](../src/services/db/database.ts#L1-L28), [app lock](../src/services/auth/useAppLock.ts#L22-L47), and [lock storage](../src/services/auth/appLockStore.ts#L30-L56).

The manual `.openlog` archive is not encrypted. A copy can remain in app cache if saving or sharing fails after export. Android system backup includes shared preferences, but the repository does not list every value that libraries can store there. The iOS configuration has no backup exclusion, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The policy did not explain Android backup behavior. [Export archive](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L125-L132), [export cleanup](../src/services/backup/export/index.ts#L320-L324), [share fallback](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L137-L171), and [backup rules](../plugins/withAndroidBackupRules.js#L12-L38).

### F4. Medium: Location, font, website, and contact requests need disclosure

A location action in the Android app sends coordinates to the native geocoder. The repository does not name its downstream provider. iOS configuration uses Core Location, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The previous policy did not describe this request. The new draft does. The provider identity remains unconfirmed. The existing review file lists this gap as P3-5. [Location service](../src/services/location/location.ts#L63-L85) and [open review finding](./review-findings.md#L9-L17).

The app also requests optional fonts from jsDelivr. GitHub Pages hosts the public website, which now uses system fonts. A person who emails the listed Gmail address sends their message and any attached files to that mailbox. The code does not define retention for website logs or email. [Font resolver](../src/services/fonts/resolver.ts#L16-L27), [site CSS](../webpage/style.css#L1), [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml#L17-L36), and [contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

### F5. Medium: Permission timing and attachment metadata need review

The app requests notification permission shortly after the timeline opens, not when a person starts a backup. Local completion notifications can show entry counts and backup size. The unused iOS configuration declares photo-library write use, but the owner confirms no iOS app has launched. The reviewed app code opens a share sheet and does not call a photo-library write API. The image path can keep the original file, so embedded metadata can remain. [Timeline prompt](../src/screens/timeline/Timeline.tsx#L17-L39), [notification content](../src/services/notifications/notifications.ts#L65-L94), [iOS permission string](../app.json#L14-L25), [image path](../src/services/media/images.ts#L11-L48), and [share action](../src/services/media/share.ts#L15-L32).

The attachment picker accepts any file type. It can open selected files in another app. The policy did not describe file-provider or share-target handling. [Document picker](../src/services/media/attachments.ts#L20-L68).

The privacy contact uses a Gmail address. The code does not define mailbox-provider retention or how the owner handles requests. [Contact address](../webpage/index.html#L15-L21).

### F6. Medium: Public claims are broader than the implementation

The README says content stays on the device and is never uploaded. The website says the app works offline. The About screen says everything stays on the device. These statements omit PostHog telemetry, geocoding, system backups, and user-selected sharing. The earlier terms also made a broad no-upload claim. The revised terms remove that claim. The prior policy promised practical notice for material changes, but the app has no in-app notice path. [README](../README.md#L7-L15), [website](../webpage/index.html#L85-L102), [About screen](../src/screens/settings/AboutSettings.tsx#L79-L84), and [terms](../webpage/terms.html#L27-L38).

The product guide says analytics never include locations. The app sends location-use and location-presence events. These events do not contain exact coordinates, so the guide and event design need a shared definition of location data. [Product guide](../AGENTS.md#L13-L16), [location event](../src/services/location/useLocation.ts#L30-L40), and [entry event fields](../src/screens/compose/Compose.tsx#L213-L224).

### F7. Medium: Retention, rights, operator, age, and jurisdiction are unknown

The app sets no local content expiry and has no single control that clears entries, profile details, preferences, font files, and analytics state. Delete-all removes entries, tags, and drafts. It tries to remove unreferenced media, but leaves profile and app preferences. SQLite deletion does not promise secure erasure. PostHog retention, website log retention, and email retention are not defined in the repository. [Delete-all action](../src/modules/entry/store/EntryStore.ts#L139-L147), [privacy settings](../src/screens/settings/PrivacySettings.tsx#L375-L386), and [database setup](../src/services/db/schema.ts#L33-L50).

The previous policy said OpenLog is not directed to children under 13, but the app does not ask for age or enforce an age limit. The owner identifies Rwitesh Bera as the individual maintainer and says no company is registered. The exact age range, full territory list, postal address, and privacy-request process remain unknown. The repository does not contain a Google Play Data Safety declaration. [Policy draft](../webpage/privacy-policy.html), [public contact and terms](../webpage/terms.html#L63-L79), [Android release workflow](../.github/workflows/release-android.yml#L1-L20), and [iOS config](../app.json#L11-L25).

## Recommendations

1. Confirm the production PostHog token, data region, GeoIP behavior, retention, processor terms, subprocessors, and deletion process.
2. Add a user-facing analytics choice or confirm that analytics run by default. Update the policy and store disclosures to match.
3. Disable launch-URL capture unless the app needs it. Add a tested event scrubber for exception text, stack traces, paths, and query values.
4. Decide whether to add encryption for local content and backup archives. Protect app-switcher snapshots before the JavaScript cover appears, or document this limit. Document Android backup behavior. Review iOS backup rules before an iOS launch. Remove temporary export files on every exit path.
5. Confirm the Android geocoder provider. Keep location use explicit and document that the platform geocoder receives coordinates.
6. Remove the unused photo-library write permission or add and document the feature that needs it. Use the narrowest photo-picker access available. Remove photo metadata before storage or explain that it can remain.
7. Move the notification prompt to a backup action. Limit completion details that appear on lock screens.
8. Confirm GitHub Pages and contact-mail retention.
9. Align the README, website, About screen, and product guide with the confirmed data flows. Keep the revised terms consistent with the Privacy Policy.
10. Define retention, deletion, and privacy-request steps. Confirm the legal operator, address, age range, user countries, supported platforms, and notice process before publication.

## Owner clarifications

1. What PostHog retention period, GeoIP configuration, data-processing terms, and subprocessor list apply? Who handles deletion requests?
2. Does the owner want automatic error and launch-link capture? What legal basis and user choice apply to analytics and location requests?
3. What postal contact address and email-retention period belong in the policy?
4. What age groups does OpenLog serve? What countries does Google Play make the app available in, and which countries are excluded?
5. What data can Android shared preferences contain? Does the owner intend Android cloud backup and device transfer?
6. Which service resolves Android coordinates? What service terms and retention apply to coordinates sent by the platform geocoder?
7. Does any supported feature save photos directly to the photo library? What rules apply to attachment metadata and files selected from cloud providers?
8. What privacy-request and notice processes does the owner use? Does any business practice share or sell data beyond the flows in this repository?

## Regulatory review

The repository does not establish the country of the operator, user countries, age range, or business thresholds. This review cannot decide which laws apply. Counsel must assess the launch markets. Candidate laws include GDPR, UK GDPR, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act of India, US state privacy laws, and COPPA. Counsel must assess COPPA if the service targets children or the owner knows a child under 13 uses it.

Use data minimization, purpose limits, retention limits, and privacy by design as review criteria. Use the NIST Privacy Framework for a follow-up privacy review and OWASP MASVS for mobile security review. Confirm Google Play Data Safety for the Android build. Review Apple App Privacy before any iOS launch. This code review does not establish compliance with any law or framework.

Edit a pull request.

Without an argument, the pull request that belongs to the current branch
is selected.

Editing a pull request's projects requires authorization with the `project` scope.
To authorize, run `gh auth refresh -s project`.

Use `--attach` to upload an image or video. Without a body flag the pull
request keeps the body it already has and the attachment is appended to it. If the
body references an attached file, such as `![alt](./login.png)`, that reference
is rewritten to point at the uploaded asset instead. Paths in a `--body-file` are
relative to its directory, falling back to the working directory.
You can attach up to 50 files per command.

Alt text for an image follows the path after `#`, as in
`--attach './login.png#The login error state'`. Without it the filename is used.
A reference already in the body keeps the alt text written there. Video renders
as a player and has no alt text, so it cannot be given any.

If some attachments upload and others fail, the pull request is still updated with the
ones that succeeded. The command then exits with a non-zero status, but the pull
request's URL is still printed to stdout.

The `--add-assignee` and `--remove-assignee` flags both support
the following special values:
- `@me`: assign or unassign yourself
- `@copilot`: assign or unassign Copilot (not supported on GitHub Enterprise Server)

The `--add-reviewer` and `--remove-reviewer` flags support
the following special value:
- `@copilot`: request or remove review from Copilot (not supported on GitHub Enterprise Server)


USAGE
  gh pr edit [<number> | <url> | <branch>] [flags]

FLAGS
      --add-assignee login      Add assigned users by their login. Use "@me" to assign yourself, or "@copilot" to assign Copilot.
      --add-label name          Add labels by name
      --add-project title       Add the pull request to projects by title
      --add-reviewer login      Add or re-request reviewers by their login. Use "@copilot" to request review from Copilot.
      --attach file             Attach an image or video file, in '<file>#<image alt text>' format
  -B, --base branch             Change the base branch for this pull request
  -b, --body string             Set the new body.
  -F, --body-file file          Read body text from file (use "-" to read from standard input)
  -m, --milestone name          Edit the milestone the pull request belongs to by name
      --remove-assignee login   Remove assigned users by their login. Use "@me" to unassign yourself, or "@copilot" to unassign Copilot.
      --remove-label name       Remove labels by name
      --remove-milestone        Remove the milestone association from the pull request
      --remove-project title    Remove the pull request from projects by title
      --remove-reviewer login   Remove reviewers by their login. Use "@copilot" to remove review request from Copilot.
  -t, --title string            Set the new title.

INHERITED FLAGS
      --help                     Show help for command
  -R, --repo [HOST/]OWNER/REPO   Select another repository using the [HOST/]OWNER/REPO format

EXAMPLES
  # Edit the title and body of a pull request
  $ gh pr edit 23 --title "I found a bug" --body "Nothing works"
  
  # Use a file as the body
  $ gh pr edit 23 --body-file body.txt
  
  # Append a screenshot to the body, with alt text after "#"
  $ gh pr edit 23 --attach './login.png#The login error state'
  
  # Append multiple files by repeating the flag
  $ gh pr edit 23 --attach ./before.png --attach ./after.png
  
  # Manage labels
  $ gh pr edit 23 --add-label "bug,help wanted" --remove-label "core"
  
  # Manage reviewers
  $ gh pr edit 23 --add-reviewer monalisa,hubot --remove-reviewer myorg/team-name
  
  # Re-request review
  $ gh pr edit 23 --add-reviewer monalisa
  
  # Request a review from GitHub Copilot
  $ gh pr edit 23 --add-reviewer "@copilot"
  
  # Manage assignees
  $ gh pr edit 23 --add-assignee "@me" --remove-assignee monalisa,hubot
  
  # Assign GitHub Copilot
  $ gh pr edit 23 --add-assignee "@copilot"
  
  # Manage projects and milestones
  $ gh pr edit 23 --add-project "Roadmap" --remove-project v1,v2
  $ gh pr edit 23 --milestone "Version 1"
  $ gh pr edit 23 --remove-milestone

LEARN MORE

content.thinking:
**Considering GitHub limitations**

GitHub retains commit objects, so we can't force garbage collection. Creating a new repository isn’t a solution here. An old commit may remain accessible via the API for up to 90 days, even if unreachable. To remove sensitive data, the user would need to contact GitHub Support, as there's no actual personally identifiable information (PII), just internal audit details. We should mention this limitation and ask if they want to pursue contacting GitHub Support for potential removal.

content.text:
I revised the Android policy and legal-page styling. The Terms page now avoids the broad no-upload claim. Both legal pages use smaller, plain headings and system fonts. The public site no longer requests Google Fonts.

The policy says PostHog analytics are active in the Android app and processed in the US. I did not call the data anonymous: an installation ID and IP address can link events to an installation and suggest an approximate region. The policy also covers location requests, backups, sharing, local storage, retention, and error reports.

The Downloads CSV shows installed-audience totals and selected country columns. It does not establish the full list of available or excluded countries, so the public policy names none.

**PR #17** is updated as a draft: [Update Android privacy policy](https://github.com/rwitesh/openlog/pull/17). The audit report is now local and ignored, not in the PR. No application code changed. The pre-existing `.codex/hooks.json` deletion remains untouched.

**One remaining limitation:** I removed the Entire checkpoints and the report from the PR’s current files. GitHub still resolves the old commit `83bd622` by SHA, so I cannot confirm that its contents are fully purged. A GitHub Support request might be needed. Would you like me to prepare one?

`pnpm test` passed (82 tests), `pnpm typecheck` and Biome passed, and the HTML and diff checks passed. I did not test on a device or emulator.
